tldr: Appendix C survey data from 30+ Oregon stakeholders (businesses, nonprofits, individuals) on economic development priorities. Dominant themes: clean energy/manufacturing as growth sectors; workforce development and prevailing wage/union standards; startup ecosystem concerns over SB 1507 retroactive taxation; regulatory and permitting complexity barriers; childcare/Preschool for All advocacy; housing affordability crisis; K–12 education reform. Respondents span market-oriented (business tax cuts, deregulation) to progressive (wealth taxes, labor protections, climate action) viewpoints.

bullets.text: Clean energy sector sustained 67,000 in-state jobs in 2023 (breakdown: 11,185 from electricity generation, 5,720 from fuels, 13,159 from transmission/distribution); advocates call for transmission authority, grid modernization, and EVs/heat pump policies modeled on Texas and California

SB 1507 imposes retroactive 9.9% state income tax on startup exits (effective January 1, 2026), creating disincentive to found/invest in Oregon; startup community warns of relocation to Washington (15 minutes away, zero state income tax) and cites need for QSBS conformity restoration

Labor standards laws HB 2021, HB 3031, HB 4059, HB 4080 codified prevailing wages, apprenticeship requirements, and targeted hiring for clean energy projects; advocates seek expansion to other sectors and stricter enforcement
Preschool for All program endorsed as 3-to-1 return-on-investment and family income booster (~22%); noted as existing model with proven outcomes, warranting expansion while maintaining quality

Permitting and regulatory complexity barrier cited across industries: seafood processors face prohibitive wastewater standards (heavy metals removal despite trace-level occurrence); construction delays; calls for pre-permit industry collaboration and economic feasibility review

Wage stagnation and inequality: 28% of Oregon jobs pay less than $20/hour, 57% less than $30/hour; top 1% wages grew 345% over four decades vs. 15% gain for average worker; multiple calls for wealth taxes, corporate tax increases, and higher minimum wage

Industrial site shortage in Portland Metro: average parcel size 2.5 acres; extremely limited sites over 20 acres; none over 50 acres; HB 4078 removal of 2,200 industrial acres projected to cost state 30,000 jobs and $6.3–$12.7B annual revenue

Housing affordability crisis: renters and homebuyers priced out despite above-minimum wages; proposals include rent freeze, affordable infill, land value tax reform, limits on NNN rent increases, and protections for commercial tenants

Education system reform priorities: ability to dismiss underperforming teachers (union protections cited as barrier); K–12 curriculum overhaul for modern economy; consolidation of districts under 500 students; school schedule alignment with working parents; college affordability and 'earn to learn' programs
